title: Work IQ: how agents reach Microsoft 365 and business data, and what an admin can switch off
summary: The documented control paths and commands check out, including the consent path and the beta spending-policy endpoints flagged by the pre-check. The blanket statement that Microsoft documents no Work IQ audit event names needs correcting: Microsoft Graph documents WorkIQAdminActivity audit records, although that does not establish which events capture individual tool invocations.

claims.claim: No admin-centre navigation path is documented for creating the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "service principal" "admin center" enable. Opened enable-work-iq and the A2A quickstart; the enablement Admin center tab directs the reader to Graph Explorer rather than a portal setting.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 creates the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7"

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API equivalent of the Work IQ MCP policy switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy block "API" PowerShell Graph. Opened policy-governance-mcp and mcp/overview; policy concepts and the portal procedure are documented, but no callable policy-management endpoint or cmdlet is given.

claims.claim: The whole Work IQ MCP server can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent of the Work IQ MCP Block control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy block "API" PowerShell Graph. Opened manage-ai-experience-access and policy-governance-mcp; neither gives a Block endpoint or cmdlet, and search returned no reference documenting one.

claims.claim: Grant and revoke consent on the app's API permissions page under Entra ID > App registrations, using Grant admin consent for [your tenant] or WorkIQAgent.Ask > Revoke admin consent.
claims.quote: go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant]. ... On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.claim: az ad app permission admin-consent --id <app-id> grants the registered app's requested admin consent.
claims.quote: Add the WorkIQAgent.Ask delegated permission and grant consent. ... az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumption and spending are managed under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The beta Cost Management API lists and creates spending policies with GET and POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies and updates them with PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... GET /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... POST /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}

claims.claim: Business Applications audience is configured in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. ... In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent of the Business Applications audience setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications data in Work IQ" PowerShell API. Opened default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; results describe the audience portal setting, not a command or API for it.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ features are configured in Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. ... Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Locate Work IQ. ... Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent of the environment Work IQ setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "environment" setting PowerShell API participation. Opened manage-participation and default-settings; the results give the Power Platform admin center procedure but no automation reference.

claims.claim: App Access Control uses Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled > Allow or Block > Save.
claims.quote: Select Enabled in the Access control dropdown list. ... Select a Dataverse application, then select one of these options, located above the grid: Allow to allow access to the app. Block to deny access to the app.
claims.fix: Insert the app-selection step: Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled > Dataverse application > Allow or Block > Save.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent of this App Access Control procedure is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "App access control" "API" PowerShell Dataverse Enabled; "App access control" "Web API" settings. Opened control-app-access-environment. Results give its UI modes and generic Web API guidance, not an API for this setting.

claims.claim: Makers select an agent's Work IQ workloads in Copilot Studio > Build > Tools > Work IQ > Edit tool > Sources.
claims.quote: On the Build tab, under Tools, select Work IQ. ... In the Edit tool dialog, review the Connection. ... Under Sources, select the workloads to use, as described in Select workloads for your agent.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of Copilot Studio's per-agent Work IQ Sources selection is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "Sources" workloads configuration API Copilot Studio. Opened use-work-iq; the results document the maker dialog, not a configuration API. Retrieve request capability scoping is a different control.

claims.claim: az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 is the CLI alternative for creating the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Create the Work IQ service principal in your organization by running the following command. ... az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7

claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through the API requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator at runtime.

claims.claim: The Business Applications audience options are All users, Specific groups and No users, with All users the default.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. ... To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default. ... To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups

claims.claim: The linked Foundry article describes preview items.
claims.quote: Items marked preview in this article are currently in preview.

claims.where: controls[6].note; Risks and limits: Participation settings do not block agents
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data; App Access controls manage that access.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: App Access Control requires a Managed Environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator can manage the application-access settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to work with application-access settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The Work IQ preview page gives a shorter App Access procedure, using Enable then Save, than the dedicated App Access reference.
claims.quote: Select the environment in which you want to enable app access. ... Select Enable, and then select Save. ... Return to the environment and select the applications you want to block from accessing the environment.

claims.where: controls[8].note; Risks and limits: Workload scoping is coarse
claims.claim: Copilot Studio's Work IQ Sources selector controls whole workloads, not individual sites or mailboxes.
claims.quote: Selection is limited to whole workloads. You can't use this setting to select individual sites, mailboxes, or other resources within a workload.

claims.claim: Selecting Work IQ workloads does not override organisational permissions or policies.
claims.quote: Selecting a workload doesn't override your organization's permissions or policies.

claims.claim: Work IQ is Microsoft's workplace intelligence layer for agents and applications to reason over organisational and business data with permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools. It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Work IQ requests run in a particular signed-in user's context.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: Work IQ exposes A2A, remote MCP and REST endpoints.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: The Chat component provides conversational intelligence through A2A and REST.
claims.quote: Chat is optimized for conversational intelligence. Work IQ supports A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration and REST for web application interactions

claims.claim: Work IQ assembles grounded context internally so agents need not manage their own retrieval pipelines.
claims.quote: Work IQ assembles and grounds context internally across organizational and business data to provide agent-ready inputs, so agents don't need to stitch together raw signals or manage retrieval pipelines.

claims.claim: Generic MCP tools act as verbs on resource paths.
claims.quote: These tools function as simple verbs (such as fetch, create, and update), while resource paths define what the agent is working with.

claims.claim: Workspaces use SharePoint Embedded working storage for intermediate data and outputs.
claims.quote: SharePoint Embedded working storage gives agents a persistent space within your Microsoft 365 tenant boundary to manage intermediate data and outputs

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview says ten generic tools.
claims.quote: collapses hundreds of operations into just 10 generic tools

claims.claim: The MCP overview's tool tables name more than ten tools.
claims.quote: Entity tools | fetch, fetch_blob, create_entity, update_entity, delete_entity, do_action, call_function ... Copilot tools | ask, retrieve, list_agents ... Schema tools | get_schema, search_paths

claims.claim: The live tools/list response is authoritative for available tools and schemas.
claims.quote: Tool availability and schemas can evolve, so use the schema returned by tools/list as the source of truth instead of hard-coding a locally copied schema.

claims.where: What it is: What it can reach
claims.claim: The API overview lists email, meetings and calendar, OneDrive and SharePoint documents, Teams messages, people, Planner plans and enterprise search results.
claims.quote: Work IQ can reason over: ... Email messages ... Meetings and calendar data ... Documents in OneDrive and SharePoint ... Microsoft Teams messages ... People and organizational context ... Microsoft Planner plans ... Enterprise search results

claims.where: What it is: What it can reach
claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ adds Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data in preview.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is a set of capabilities that lets Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients work with Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data. ... This is a preview feature.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Application-only authentication is not supported.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ evaluates MCP requests using Rego, Open Policy Agent's policy language.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules. ... It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: MCP policy complements rather than replaces Entra authentication, OAuth permissions and the user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided; Why it matters
claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: Work IQ is added by default to every new Copilot Studio agent using the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Work IQ is generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio and is added by default to every new agent that uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not repair oversharing in SharePoint or mailboxes.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "oversharing"; "Work IQ" "oversharing" SharePoint permissions. Opened the Work IQ overview, API overview and policy page. They document permission trimming and policy, not whether Work IQ repairs oversharing.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical product claim with analysis tied to the documented premise: 'Because access is user-scoped, review existing SharePoint and mailbox permissions rather than treating Work IQ policy as a substitute for that review.'

claims.claim: Tenant MCP policy can narrow paths, operations and collection traversal.
claims.quote: For example, a tenant policy can allow read access to common productivity data while blocking high-risk paths, write operations, or large collection traversal.

claims.where: Why it matters: defaults; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot Studio page states that write operations are on by default subject to organisational permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.

claims.where: Why it matters: defaults; Open questions
claims.claim: The MCP policy page states that mutation operations including sending email are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Default enablement for non-excepted new Business Applications environments starts on 30 September 2026.
claims.quote: Starting September 30, 2026, Microsoft turns on these capabilities by default for all new environments that aren't listed as exceptions in this article.

claims.claim: Default enablement for non-excepted existing environments starts in November 2026.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.

claims.claim: Default enablement applies to public production environments subject to the source's listed exceptions.
claims.quote: The default applies to public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions: ... European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments ... Government-related environments ... Nonproduction environments

claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users
claims.claim: Work IQ remains subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users
claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence are billed based on usage.
claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spending policies; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot Studio page says Work IQ does not require a separate spending policy.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses consumption billing. A separate spending policy isn't required for Work IQ.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spending policies; Open questions
claims.claim: The public-preview retrieve page requires calling users to belong to a spending policy including Work IQ API.
claims.quote: The retrieve tool is available in public preview. ... Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The Foundry page also requires Copilot Credits billing and a Work IQ API spending policy for retrieve.
claims.quote: For retrieve, also complete the retrieve prerequisites, including Copilot Credits billing and a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The Work IQ pages do not publish a numerical per-request credit rate.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "credit" "rate" pricing per request; "Work IQ" pricing "Tool" "Credits"; "Work IQ" "licensing" "rate". Opened the Work IQ overview, API overview, retrieve and Business Applications understand-costs; none states a numerical per-request rate.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ can use extra storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policy is tenant-wide only
claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. ... When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policy is tenant-wide only; Open questions
claims.claim: Initial MCP policy has no per-user, per-app, per-agent or scenario-specific policy templates.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy denial looks like a failure
claims.claim: Tenant policy can deny an authenticated request even when the app has the required OAuth permission.
claims.quote: an MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policy set too early can fail
claims.claim: Configuring policy before first MCP use can fail because the service principal has not yet been created, and manual enablement provisions it.
claims.quote: such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail. Tenant administrators can provision it by following the steps in Enable your tenant for Work IQ.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Business Applications in Work IQ is preview and not for government clouds
claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is unavailable in sovereign or government clouds including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Business Applications in Work IQ is preview and not for government clouds
claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ may move data outside a FedRAMP-accredited environment's authorisation boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Multitenant organisations can fail to authenticate
claims.claim: In multitenant organisations the token issuer must match the signed-in user's home tenant rather than merely the app-registration tenant.
claims.quote: In multitenant (parent/child) organizations, the access token's issuer (iss) must match the tenant the signed-in user belongs to, not the tenant where the app is registered.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Multitenant organisations can fail to authenticate
claims.claim: Using the wrong tenant authentication configuration causes a 400 AuthenticationError.
claims.quote: Register the app as multitenant (AzureADMultipleOrgs) and have users sign in through their home tenant's authority. Otherwise, the request fails with 400 AuthenticationError: "Error authenticating with resource".

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator manages Business Applications participation settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.claim: Environment Maker or System Customizer configures application-level participation.
claims.quote: Environment Maker or System Customizer role to configure application-level participation.

claims.claim: Business Applications sharing settings cascade through tenant, environment and app levels.
claims.quote: You manage Business Applications in Work IQ through a cascading set of settings at three levels: ... Microsoft 365 admin center (tenant level) ... Power Platform admin center (environment level) ... Power Apps maker portal (app level)

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant sharing setting stops Copilot Chat and Dataverse sharing even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: How they interact
claims.claim: The MCP server availability control applies to the whole server separately from Copilot audience settings and App Access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: Enabling environment Work IQ features is a separate decision from allowing Work IQ to reason over its data.
claims.quote: Enabling these features in an environment is a separate decision from allowing Work IQ to reason over that environment's data.

claims.claim: No separate configuration path is documented for environment data participation as distinct from environment feature enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "data participation" configure environment. Opened manage-participation and default-settings. The former distinguishes decisions but supplies no separate data-participation procedure; the latter gives the existing Work IQ feature toggle.

claims.claim: Microsoft says every Work IQ tool invocation is logged and evaluated.
claims.quote: Every tool invocation is logged and evaluated, enabling auditability, usage analytics, rate limiting, and real-time compliance enforcement across agents and data sources.

claims.claim: No Work IQ audit event name is documented.
claims.quote: Audit data for Work IQ Admin Activity events returned in the auditData property of an auditLogRecord.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket absence with: 'Microsoft Graph documents WorkIQAdminActivity admin audit records. The Work IQ pages do not identify the operation names that capture individual tool invocations.' Cite this resource and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/security-auditlogrecordtype?view=graph-rest-1.0, whose enum includes WorkIQAdminActivity. Do not equate admin activity with tool-invocation coverage.

claims.where: Governance controls: Not enforced; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated Work IQ tool-invocation audit report path is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" audit event Purview report tool invocations; "Work IQ" "audit" "invocations"; "Work IQ" "audit" "report". Opened Work IQ overview and Graph workIQAdminActivity; no dedicated tool-invocation audit-report path was documented.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center allow/disallow tooling and MCP server controls might not yet be available in every region.
claims.quote: The ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not be available in your region yet.

claims.claim: Microsoft says more granular MCP policy controls and templates might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.where: Governance controls: How they interact; controls
claims.claim: The prose identifies a separate environment data-participation decision with no documented path, but the controls table does not show that gap.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ features in an environment is a separate decision from allowing Work IQ to reason over its data; no separate path is documented at the time of writing. ... Work IQ feature enablement for a Dataverse environment
claims.fix: Add an environment-scoped row for 'Whether Work IQ may reason over and return environment data', with both surfaces null and a note distinguishing the documented participation decision from feature enablement, citing manage-participation.
